title: Tight instances of the Lonely Runner Conjecture: one-entry modifications and the growth of speeds
summary: For a set $V$ of $n-1$ distinct positive integers let $\mathrm{LR}(V)=\max_{t}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. The Lonely Runner Conjecture asserts $\mathrm{LR}(V)\ge 1/n$, and $V$ is called tight if equality holds. Goddyn and Wong determined which of the sets obtained from $[n-1]=\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ by multiplying a single entry by an integer are tight.
